open_points.subject: FlowVersion persistence and acyclicity
open_points.text: State 0 says “the version is kept either way” when proof fails, while M13 defines a FlowVersion as “One immutable, acyclic graph of a flow.”
open_points.question: When a submitted graph is cyclic, is it retained as an unproven FlowVersion, or refused before a FlowVersion exists?
options: Retain cyclic submissions as unproven FlowVersions
Refuse cyclic submissions before creating a FlowVersion
Retain them under a separate candidate model
open_points.default_guess: Retain the submitted graph as an unproven FlowVersion, because State 0 explicitly says the version is kept when proof fails.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity and dependency changes
open_points.text: M17 says “proving the same version gives the same result,” but the carried decision says a version that failed because its binding was not accepted may be proven again after acceptance and then succeed.
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult identified by the flow version alone, or by the flow version together with the dependency state or resulting proof facts at the time of proof?
options: One mutable/current result per flow version
A distinct value for each different set of proof-result facts
A result keyed by flow version plus a snapshot or revision of proof dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Treat each different set of proof-result facts as a distinct value computed on demand; a flow version alone does not determine the result.
